title: The count needs polynomial-calculus degree n^{Omega(1)} over every field
claim: Over every field, every polynomial-calculus refutation of the octahedral knot sphere's NAE formula NAE(K_k) (n = 4k^2 points) has degree at least c n^{1/4}/log n: the functional pigeonhole principle on a bipartite boundary expander with N + 1 pigeons, N holes, left degree 3 and hole degree O(log N) (Miksa and Nordstrom, Theorem 4.9: degree linear in N over every field) reduces to LeftPigeon_N by decision trees reading a pointer in at most max(3, hole degree) queries, hence through COUNT-SYSTEMS-20261110-001A's chain to the count with n = O(N^4), and polynomial-calculus degree transfers through decision-tree reductions at a cost of the trees' depth. Over F2, with TREE-XOR-20261110-001B, tree-like Res(xor) refutations of the count have size at least 2^{c n^{1/4}/log n}, and parity decision trees for it have depth at least c n^{1/4}/log n.
failure_conditions: A LeftPigeon answer of the reduction that decodes to no falsified clause of FPHP_G, or reads more than 3 + max(3, hole degree) variables.
A counterclockwise full triangle of the composed chain that decodes to no falsified clause of FPHP_G.
foundation_claim_scope: The octahedral knot sphere's Kasteleyn-signed NAE formula NAE(K_k); proof complexity of its refutations.

validation.status: proved by hand from Miksa and Nordstrom's degree bound and the program's reductions; the new reduction step and its composition checked by check.py
validation.novelty: known-with-delta (folklore risk high): FPHP on expanders is hard for the polynomial calculus over every field and lies in PPADS^dt; no published statement of a polynomial-calculus degree bound for a PPADS-complete principle or for this formula was found in a bounded search
